title: At the Iron Gate  (Junto a la verja de hierro)

segments.t: Afuera, bajo la sombra del árbol en la posada Linden Courtyard Inn, en Portland, el hermano mayor, Owen, permanece erguido con su abrigo gris frente a Caleb mientras Hannah deja una tetera caliente y se retira un paso. Escucha primero toda la escena.
So 'someone with something from Grandfather' was you all along, Caleb.
Hello, Owen. Thank you for coming today.
I recognized your neat block handwriting on that postcard in two seconds.
Wait, you knew it was from me and came anyway?
Of course I came. Why did you hide behind a mystery note?
Because I was afraid you were still angry. I missed you these three years.
Three stubborn years... honestly, little brother, I missed you too.
Excuse me, gentlemen. Here is hot tea, and warm lemon cake is on the way.
Lemon cake? Wait, how did she know about Friday lemon cake?
Sit down, Owen, take off your heavy coat, and look at this blue suitcase.
Is that the old dark blue bag from Grandfather's workshop?
Take all the time you need. The courtyard is yours.
Ahora repasemos la conversación con calma, frase por frase.
So 'someone with something from Grandfather' was you all along, Caleb.
'Así que alguien con algo del abuelo eras tú todo el tiempo, Caleb.' Observa cómo
was you all along
mantiene el verbo en tercera persona porque el sujeto gramatical es 'alguien'.
Hello, Owen. Thank you for coming today.
'Hola, Owen. Gracias por venir hoy.' La primera frase sencilla de Hannah funciona al instante:
Thank you for coming today
directa y cálida.
I recognized your neat block handwriting on that postcard in two seconds.
'Reconocí tu letra limpia de imprenta en esa postal en dos segundos.' Para escribir con letras sueltas sin enlazar, el inglés usa
block handwriting
letra de molde.
Wait, you knew it was from me and came anyway?
'Espera, ¿sabías que era mía y viniste de todos modos?' Al final de la frase,
came anyway
expresa 'viniste pese a todo, de todas formas'.
Of course I came. Why did you hide behind a mystery note?
'Por supuesto que vine. ¿Por qué te escondiste detrás de una nota misteriosa?' Para confirmar con rotundidad se une
Of course I came
sin ninguna conjunción en medio.
Because I was afraid you were still angry. I missed you these three years.
'Porque tenía miedo de que siguieras enfadado. Te eché de menos estos tres años.' Donde decimos 'tenía miedo de que', el inglés usa 'be' más adjetivo:
I was afraid
y sigue directo con la frase.
Three stubborn years... honestly, little brother, I missed you too.
'Tres años cabezotas... sinceramente, hermanito, yo también te eché de menos.' El cierre afectuoso
I missed you too
sella la reconciliación con total sencillez.
Excuse me, gentlemen. Here is hot tea, and warm lemon cake is on the way.
'Disculpen, caballeros. Aquí tienen té caliente, y el pastel tibio de limón viene de camino.' Muy útil en restaurantes y entregas:
is on the way
ya viene en camino.
Lemon cake? Wait, how did she know about Friday lemon cake?
'¿Pastel de limón? Espera, ¿cómo sabía ella lo del pastel de limón de los viernes?' Para saber de la existencia de un detalle o secreto se combina
know about
saber acerca de.
Sit down, Owen, take off your heavy coat, and look at this blue suitcase.
'Siéntate, Owen, quítate tu abrigo pesado y mira esta maleta azul.' Para quitarse prendas de ropa o zapatos usamos siempre el verbo con partícula
take off
quitarse.
Is that the old dark blue bag from Grandfather's workshop?
'¿Esa es la vieja bolsa azul oscuro del taller del abuelo?' Fíjate en el posesivo con apóstrofo en
Grandfather's workshop
el taller del abuelo.
Take all the time you need. The courtyard is yours.
'Tómense todo el tiempo que necesiten. El patio es suyo.' Dos expresiones llenas de hospitalidad:
Take all the time you need
y el posesivo final
is yours
es de ustedes. Escuchemos otra vez toda la escena a velocidad natural.
So 'someone with something from Grandfather' was you all along, Caleb.
Hello, Owen. Thank you for coming today.
I recognized your neat block handwriting on that postcard in two seconds.
Wait, you knew it was from me and came anyway?
Of course I came. Why did you hide behind a mystery note?
Because I was afraid you were still angry. I missed you these three years.
Three stubborn years... honestly, little brother, I missed you too.
Excuse me, gentlemen. Here is hot tea, and warm lemon cake is on the way.
Lemon cake? Wait, how did she know about Friday lemon cake?
Sit down, Owen, take off your heavy coat, and look at this blue suitcase.
Is that the old dark blue bag from Grandfather's workshop?
Take all the time you need. The courtyard is yours.
Owen reconoció la letra de Caleb en dos segundos y vino de todos modos. En la próxima escena abren el paquete de papel blanco bajo el árbol del patio. Hasta la próxima.
See you soon!
